scope: Current factual package for the dangerous Mort'ton combat and skilling minigame. It covers the temple, sacred-oil, cremation, catacomb, chest, and permanent-unlock chains. It proposes integration records only; it does not choose a route, target a chest count, or infer an account result.

included: quest access, current transport alternatives, temple repair resources, shared Repair State, personal Sanctity, sacred oil, pyre-log, cremation, key, chest, lock, door, and reward mechanics
the deterministic versus RNG boundary for temple conversions, shade drops, cremation outcomes, chest loot, unique rewards, and permanent recipe or storage unlocks
current diary links, local danger and death rules, team/attention boundaries, and explicit account-observation requirements
proposed facts, actions, nodes, edges, and observed account fields for central integration
excluded: whether to rush the minigame, choose a world, use Temple Trekking, farm a particular shade tier, pursue Zealot's robes, or stop at any target
any assumed temple condition, Sanctity, materials, sacred oil, pyre logs, kills, shade remains, keys, doors, chest loot, coins, XP, recipes, collection-log result, death, or combat readiness
expected keys, rates, time, profit, XP, supplies, or success claims from any community setup or guide
automatic readiness, equipment replacement, banking, travel, or loss/reclaim transitions

location_and_transport: Mort'ton teleport and the post-quest Shades of Mort'ton minigame teleport are direct options with their own item/cooldown observations.
Fairy ring BKR then Swamp Boaty; Canifis/Myreque-base shortcut then Swamp Boaty; Morytania legs 3 or 4 to Burgh de Rott then run north; and Barrows Teleport are factual alternatives.
The Shade Catacombs entrance is north-west of Mort'ton. Entering deeper areas requires a player-held key that opens the relevant door tier; doors do not consume that key.
Hard Temple Trekking/Burgh de Rott Ramble can expose Fiyr shades as an alternative encounter route. It does not grant a key, remain, combat success, or safe bypass automatically.

temple_and_sanctity.shared_repair_state: The temple Repair State is shared between players and falls as shades attack. The current global state must be observed, never assumed from a plan or a past visit.
temple_and_sanctity.personal_resources: Each compatible material set consumes 1 beam or plank, 1 limestone brick, and 5 swamp paste and adds 5 percent to the player's personal Resources counter.
temple_and_sanctity.personal_sanctity: Starts at 0 percent, is gained by temple work or nearby shade kills, decays by 1 percent per minute, and resets to 0 on logout. Approximate source figures are 5 percent Sanctity per 1 percent resources spent and 2 percent per nearby shade kill; live results still require observation.
temple_and_sanctity.reset_state: During a temple-reset phase, repairs may be outpaced by decay. Treat it as an observed current state, not an action failure that destroys account items or history.
temple_and_sanctity.lighting: A fully repaired temple can be lit at the fire altar. Lit status is shared/current and must be observed before sanctification.

conversion_chain.input: olive oil at a lit altar with at least 10 percent observed Sanctity
conversion_chain.cost: 0.9 percent Sanctity per oil dose; 4-dose vial costs 3.6 percent
conversion_chain.boundary: Use of the altar does not claim availability, sufficient Sanctity, or an unchanged global temple state without account observation.

conversion_chain.input: Serum 207 at a lit altar with at least 20 percent observed Sanctity
conversion_chain.boundary: A Serum 208 use can be permanent only when an observed dose is used on Razmire or Ulsquire; other afflicted cures are temporary and their small rewards are RNG/observed.

conversion_chain.deterministic_output: matching pyre logs and 5 Firemaking XP per sacred-oil dose consumed
conversion_chain.requirements: Normal/Achey 5 Firemaking and 2 doses; oak 20/2; willow 35/3; teak 40/3; arctic pine 47/2; maple 50/3; mahogany 55/3; yew 65/4; magic 80/4; redwood 95/4. Current Sailing-era log types must be sourced separately before an automated log table expands beyond this confirmed minigame table.
conversion_chain.boundary: Make-all and automatic continued sanctification are interface conveniences, not permission to infer input stock, output count, XP, or selected tier.

shade_and_cremation.cremation: At Mort'ton funeral pyres, a tinderbox plus selected compatible pyre log and selected remains completes one cremation. Prayer XP depends on the observed shade/log pairing. Morytania Hard gives 50 percent more cremation Prayer XP and Morytania Elite gives 50 percent more pyre-log Firemaking XP; neither diary infers a burn or XP outcome.
shade_and_cremation.key_or_coin_rng: Each remains has a 0.21 probability of coins; otherwise it yields a key. Loar and Urium yield their single key-metal tier. Phrin, Riyl, Asyn, and Fiyr can yield one of two metal tiers according to their trim tables. Key/coin identity, count, value, pickup, and five-minute pedestal despawn are observed events.
shade_and_cremation.death_and_failure: This is a dangerous activity. Death can create a grave and removes Hardcore Ironman status. Combat loss, kill result, remains, current location, and recovery must be reported; no combat success or death is inferred from entering Mort'ton or a catacomb.

catacomb_and_chest_loop.doors: Bronze opens bronze; steel opens steel and bronze; black opens black and below; silver opens silver and below; gold opens every door. Door opening does not consume a key. A key needs to be retained to return after leaving/dying.
catacomb_and_chest_loop.chests: A matching metal-and-lock-colour key opens a matching chest and is consumed. Every chest outcome is RNG and observed. Key trim quality ranks Red < Brown < Crimson < Black < Purple for valuable-loot probability within a metal tier.
catacomb_and_chest_loop.tiered_loot: Bronze: steel-to-mithril and easy clues; steel: steel-to-adamant and medium clues; black: black-to-adamant and medium clues; silver: black-to-rune and hard clues; gold: adamant-to-dragon, elite clues, and Zealot's robes. Chests may also provide coins, runes, armour, swamp paste, fine cloth, locks, or special rewards depending on their tables.
catacomb_and_chest_loop.repeatability: Temple repair, oil conversion, pyre production, combat, cremation, door use, and chest opening are repeatable only while the observed inputs/current state remain valid. No currency or automatic reward counter is created by this package.

dependencies_and_bypasses.detail: Only explicit activity gate; completion unlocks participation and minigame teleport.
Sacred-oil/Serum conversion requires a currently fully repaired and lit altar plus personal current Sanctity; shared temple state is not player-owned.
1 beam/plank + 1 limestone brick + 5 swamp paste is the deterministic repair-resource input.
Optional temple tools; they improve work flow but do not replace materials, live temple state, or account observations.
Gives 50 percent more Prayer XP from cremating shades; it is not key or loot protection.
Gives 50 percent more Firemaking XP from creating pyre logs; it is not oil, key, or loot protection.
Progressively open their own and lower catacomb door tiers while retained.
A retained gold key opens every catacomb door, bypassing the need to hold lower-tier door keys; it does not bypass chest-key consumption or make gold chest loot deterministic.
Possible alternative source of Fiyr remains that can make silver/gold key progression obtainable. Encounter, kill, remains, and keys stay observed/RNG.
Shades are undead, so independently observed Salve gear can improve combat; it does not prove combat readiness.
Reading observed Swampbark/Bloodbark scrolls permanently unlocks their recipe capability, while actual armour crafting has separate hard gates.
Gold chests can roll the four untradeable robe pieces. RNG does not establish ownership, full-set completion, or bone saving.

logout_or_idle_constraints: Sanctity decays 1 percent per minute and resets on logout.
Temple Repair State is shared and can decay/enter a reset state while the player is inactive.
Combat aggro, material repair, altar conversions, selected cremations, catacomb combat/doors, and chest clicks need direct input and can create dangerous outcomes.
No source-backed fixed AFK interval or reliable low-attention classification is asserted.
afk_and_attention.source_boundary: Some portions can be batch-processed with make-all/continuous altar actions, but the whole chain is not modeled as AFK. Player-reported world, inventory, and batching methods remain strategy candidates.

community_strategy_observations.claim: Players use official World 377 or coordinate groups to make temple rebuilding easier, especially at lower combat levels.
community_strategy_observations.boundary: World population, team behavior, temple condition, player safety, material cost, and outcome vary; no world selection is a route instruction.

community_strategy_observations.claim: Some Ironmen use a hard Temple Trekking route from Burgh de Rott to seek Fiyr remains and a first higher-tier key, then retain a gold key to re-enter all catacomb areas.
community_strategy_observations.boundary: The factual alternative encounter and gold-door capability are included. Encounter frequency, kill success, key odds, travel choice, and suitability are not guaranteed.

community_strategy_observations.claim: Players often batch oil, pyre logs, remains, keys, and chests using a Flamtaer bag, coffin, log basket, teleports, prayer supplies, and alchemy.
community_strategy_observations.boundary: Item ownership, inventory capacity, safety, exact batch size, time, and any profit/XP claim need player observations and strategy scoring.

community_strategy_observations.claim: Some players delay Zealot's-robe pursuit until high Firemaking/Woodcutting and gold-key access, while others pursue bark scrolls or collection-log rewards earlier.
community_strategy_observations.boundary: Gold chests are factually the Zealot's source, but target tier, stop condition, expected keys, and priority are future scoring choices.

state_boundaries: Quest completion, access, transport capability, current physical location, current temple state, personal Sanctity, materials, oil, logs, and combat readiness are distinct states.
Shared Repair State and altar-lit condition must be recorded as a current observation; neither persists as an account-owned unlock simply because another player repaired the temple.
Sanctity is per player, temporary, decays over time, and resets on logout. It cannot be derived from materials, elapsed time, a guide, or a prior repair session.
Every shade kill, remains drop, cremation, key/coin reward, key pickup, chest result, lock, unique, clue, zealot spawn, collection-log update, and XP amount is an observed event.
Door keys are reusable for doors but chest keys are consumed. Retaining a high-tier key must be observed; an action that opens a chest cannot silently preserve it.
Recipe knowledge from a read runescroll is permanent, but components, Runecraft levels, altars, runes, crafted armour, wear state, and spell effects require independent observations.
Danger, actual deaths, graves, Lost Hardcore status, reclaim, food/prayer use, and combat success cannot be inferred from a planned activity or minigame access.
Diary completion modifies the relevant observed XP event only. It does not create cremations, pyre logs, keys, oil, or readiness.

account_observations.rule: Current-state and event-reporting only. Validators may enforce ranges/non-negative counts but never derive progress or inventory.
No loot, stored count, or retained key is implied by activity participation.
Each chest output, recipe read, collection-log tick, and Zealot piece is individually report-only.
Use existing generic combat observation for attempts, time, supplies, deaths, and combat result only when supplied by the player. Do not derive readiness from combat level, a weapon, or a plan.

conflicts_and_unknowns.detail: The game title is Shades of Mort'ton. This package filename intentionally follows the requested `shades-of-mortton.json` path. Canonical production identifiers should choose one explicit apostrophe-free spelling and alias the other.

Current general Firemaking sources list newer log types, but the complete authoritative minigame compatibility table captured here confirms normal through redwood. Do not invent an extended shade-compatibility table until a current source explicitly connects each newer log to Shades of Mort'ton.

Chest and key probability tables are extensive and some public rates are estimated. This package stores tiered availability and preserves all results as RNG observations instead of auto-generating a reward expectation.
Repair State is shared, while Sanctity/resources are per-player and transient. Central integration needs a current-state snapshot convention rather than durable account fields or route prerequisites.
This package references existing Morytania diary utility facts by descriptive id. Confirm actual production ids before graph insertion and keep diary reward claims separate from observed XP events.
